key_insight: Proof novelty depends on what is measured: dependency-based distances best match intuitive differences, while semantic measures can identify the same witness in very different arguments.
engineering_relevance: Multi-level proof dissimilarity profiles could help deduplicate AI-generated proofs, coordinate prover agents, and connect unfamiliar proofs to human-understandable arguments.
method: Define 19 dissimilarity measures across 6 families and propose 10 desirable properties.
Compare syntactic, structural, dependency, semantic, information-theoretic, and higher-categorical views of proofs.
Evaluate in a Curry–Howard kernel and replicate in Lean 4/Mathlib.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covers 5 kernel-checked proofs of infinitely many primes and a Lean/Mathlib replication with 3 theorems, 19 proofs, and 18 measures; dependency-closure measures track intuition best.
watch_item: The evaluation is small, and citation-based proofs can look unlike the arguments they cite, complicating automated novelty judgments.
paper_title: How Far Apart Are Two Proofs? Measuring Proof Dissimilarity in a Proof Kernel and in Lean/Mathlib
